description: Build-time value invention and setup-time polygon geometry feeding a right-hand side, under every compiler. Each document's producer inputs are constant factors held in the document itself (unknowns defined by array `const` nodes, esm-spec §4.2), so no caller data is involved: a `distinct` producer over a ragged set whose size a state integrates, an `argmin` arg-witness buffer a state gathers through, a bin-skolem candidate-pair set a state counts, an `intersect_polygon` clip of two const rings whose area drives a state, and `polygon_intersection_area` over rings of different vertex counts. Before this tier, Julia refused the ragged, arg-witness and clip documents under both compilers and failed the unequal-ring documents with a shape-promotion conflict, and Rust's native compiler refused the arg-witness gather.

scope_excluded.go: No simulator and no inline-test runner, so a tier that DRIVES one cannot be run here (API_SPEC.md §3, capability profiles). This is an exclusion from the CATEGORY, not from the rule.
scope_excluded.typescript: No simulator and no inline-test runner, so a tier that DRIVES one cannot be run here (API_SPEC.md §3, capability profiles). This is an exclusion from the CATEGORY, not from the rule.

tolerances.detail: Most states have a constant rate over one unit of time, so their values are exact up to the integrator's rounding; the clip document's tracer decays as exp(-t), so the band covers three integrator families at a 1e-12 tolerance. The absolute floor covers a zero expectation.

named_exclusions.reason: Python's native compiler has no form for a ragged contracted range (the bound depends on the enclosing output index through its `offsets` factor) and refuses D(area_eff) by name. Python native is outside the phase-4 plan; its interpreter answers.
